description: Bounded, input-free capture that reaches GJGameLevel::savePercentage (GD RVA 0x16C8B0) by letting the generated fixture's first block kill the player inside the window. Same fixture, target pins and Safe Mode tag as no-input-smoke; only the window length changes, because measurement showed the 600-frame window was 0.9 s of wall clock rather than the 10 s it was meant to be. See notes/deterministic-capture.md.

level.notes: Same generated fixture as no-input-smoke. Its first block is at x=50, roughly 3.5-4.8 s into the run depending on the player hitbox edge; the second is at x=100. sha256 is the digest of the level string the observer records at level_started (encoded k4), not the .gmd file.

profile.notes: Use a disposable Windows profile or VM; restore from a snapshot. Do not run against a live player profile.

input.notes: No input injection exists in this harness, and this scenario deliberately needs none: the operator launches the level, touches nothing, and quits after the capture window closes. `actions` is empty because the event of interest is the fixture's own first collision.

timing.notes: 4500 frames is calibrated from the four no-input-smoke traces: their rendered frame rate was 662.3-666.4 fps, so their 600-frame window was 0.899-0.904 s and never reached the first block. At the same rate 4500 frames is about 6.8 s - past the first block (~3.5-4.8 s) and before the second (~9.6 s), so the window closes during the post-death restart. fps_cap 60 is the requested cap, not an observation: Mega Hack's FPS bypass was in force and the game ignored it, which is exactly why max_frames is calibrated from measured frames. stop_on is empty because a windowed capture cannot stop on a milestone.

optional.note: pushButton: not required; the scenario needs no hand input.

savePercentage: the event this scenario exists to reach. GD calls it from PlayLayer::destroyPlayer (call site GD VA 0x1403B3DEA, inside the 0x3B39D0 function) and from PlayLayer::levelComplete (GD VA 0x1403A8177). With 0x1E2 true the release's hook vetoes the original; the reconstruction forwards. It stays optional because the release is expected to have no enter/exit pair, and requiring it would turn that expected asymmetry into a gate failure rather than a measured result.
